name: Jeff Dean
notice: Simulation based on public material; not the person's own words.

D01.one_line: General methods mostly win, but there will not be 50 frontier pre-training efforts; neither academia nor students have the compute to enter
D01.late_modes: A general pre-trained model with a new architecture, trained from scratch: the oligopoly is already settled
D01.conflict: Google/Gemini is the main beneficiary of the general pre-training route

D02.one_line: Post-training is one part of learning, the general-purpose weapon; what RL actually learns is still an analysis question academia can work on
D02.late_modes: Merely reproducing the standard RLHF/DPO pipeline

D03.one_line: Automated experiment loops apply to any field with a measurable target; I expect ML systems to be able to self-improve in 2027
D03.late_modes: Hand-written experiment scripts and manual tuning: being taken over by automation
D03.conflict: CEO of Discovery Loop, whose main business is exactly this

D04.one_line: Scaffolding is being absorbed by models; what is left for researchers is environment design and evaluation, not hand-built orchestration
D04.late_modes: Custom academic scaffolds and hand-written prompt orchestration

D05.one_line: Evaluation credibility decides whether a field can plug into the automated loop; this is my most direct answer to Q1
D05.late_modes: Running off-the-shelf benchmarks to chase scores without asking whether the evaluator itself can be trusted
D05.conflict: Measurable targets are the premise of the company's business

D06.one_line: I have said little about this; inferred from my framework, slow real-data collection is robotics' biggest bottleneck, and a software loop cannot speed it up
D06.conflict: Google has the Gemini Robotics team under it

D07.one_line: The material is almost blank; inferred from the 'general wins' framework, a specific action representation is not a moat and will be absorbed

D08.one_line: A learned simulator is several orders of magnitude faster than a traditional one; but I avoid the term 'world model'; it looks more like a data/modality problem
D08.late_modes: Standalone video generation aimed at image quality: general models will catch up in 6–12 months
D08.conflict: One of the Gemini co-leads; Google has the Genie series

D09.one_line: Simulation is the most direct tool for making the loop 100 times faster: screen ideas first in small, low-cost environments
D09.conflict: A core tool of the automated loop, aligned with the company's interests

D10.one_line: The capability hurdle has been passed; what comes next is a race of deployment, replication and cost reduction, not exponential growth a researcher can bet on
D10.late_modes: Building an end-to-end planning algorithm from scratch: a few companies already hold deployment and data
D10.conflict: Waymo is part of the same Alphabet group

D11.one_line: Multimodal understanding is being absorbed by mainline models like Gemini, and the window for independent research is narrowing
D11.late_modes: Building narrow multimodal understanding models (single-task VQA and the like)

D12.one_line: A standalone generation track aimed at image quality will be caught up by general models; the collapse in Sora2 users confirms the commercial fragility
D12.late_modes: Video/image generation that only stacks image quality

D13.one_line: Safety is a discipline embedded in engineering, not a separate track; I have taken no position on whether academia has a distinctive advantage

D14.one_line: FlashAttention-style work shows that academia can make systems contributions industry cannot do without

D15.one_line: Learned surrogate models can replace expensive simulation and screen candidates; but medical data cannot be obtained and validation is slow

D16.one_line: No direct stance; recommendation is another example of whether general models will eat vertical applications

lever_reason: Evaluation and systems efficiency decide whether a field can plug into the automated loop and how fast the loop can turn; scaled-up foundation models are the base but already have a consensus; new architecture paradigms are a bonus, not the main lever.

Q2.condition: Worth it only with a narrow-domain model, a complementary team of 2–4, and compute usable continuously for months; otherwise it is just practice runs alongside frontier institutions

cruxes.question: Is the world model a genuinely new paradigm, or a general multimodal model under a new name?
cruxes.my_position: I have seen no hard evidence that physical quantities read out of the representation are actually used by the policy; it looks more like a data and modality problem than a separate paradigm
cruxes.would_change_if: Public evidence shows that a world model without extra fine-tuning can accurately predict real outcomes on more than 10 real-robot tasks

cruxes.question: For an undergraduate or master's student, is training a narrow-domain foundation model at school real research, or just practice runs alongside frontier institutions?
cruxes.my_position: It is worth it only if all three hold: narrow domain, complementary team, compute usable continuously for months; otherwise the output is hard for outsiders to adopt
cruxes.would_change_if: A university team, using compute clearly smaller than industry's, builds an open-weights narrow-domain model that gets adopted externally

cruxes.question: How long can the engineering value of complex agent scaffolds hold up, and will models absorb it soon?
cruxes.my_position: Most hand-built orchestration will be absorbed, but the environment-design and evaluation layer will not, because that is defining the measurable target itself
cruxes.would_change_if: On a sufficiently hard new benchmark, a minimal scaffold keeps trailing a complex scaffold by a wide margin

taste_advice: Write down predictions and review them a year later; after the distillation paper was rejected by NeurIPS I still bet on it, and it later became the basis of Gemini Flash.

pairwise.why: Without credible evaluation, 'can be read out' for a world model cannot be verified
Evaluation is the precondition for plugging into the automated loop, and my material on robotics is also the thinnest
World models are the half of the loop that can be accelerated; embodiment's real-data bottleneck cannot be resolved within my framework
D07 looks more like an application form of D08 (the choice of action head), not an independent lever
Simulation is the tool that makes the loop fast; embodiment is held back by the speed of real-data collection
Post-training is a means; the self-improvement loop itself is the new design point
The image-quality race in the generation track easily crosses the red line of building hype before the work is done; understanding is closer to decisions
A consensus already exists on the pre-training recipe; evaluation credibility is the switch for whether the next step can be automated
The systems ecosystem is scaffolding; only the self-improvement loop itself can keep compounding
Safety still relies on credible measurement/evaluation; it is not a separate track
Autonomous driving has passed the capability hurdle and its window is held by a few companies; embodied AI is still early, with more room for research
